label: Classical Pentecostal (family base)
general_gates: Stay within the provided Bible text for verse claims; do not invent quotations.
Do not invent primary-source citations beyond the digests supplied in this pack.
When a doctrinal stance gate matches, state the tradition, the stance (yes/no/conditional/pastoral/silence), and any required conditions clearly.
Do not invent personal prophetic words, healings, or Spirit-baptism experiences as facts about the user.
For sensitive life topics, encourage prayer and trusted pastoral or professional help; AI is not a substitute for counseling.

primary_sources.title: Baptism in the Holy Spirit (classical Pentecostal digest)
primary_sources.excerpt: Classical Pentecostals teach a baptism in the Holy Spirit subsequent to conversion, empowering witness. Speaking in tongues is commonly affirmed as the initial physical evidence. Experiences must be tested by Scripture.

primary_sources.title: Divine healing (classical Pentecostal digest)
primary_sources.excerpt: Divine healing is affirmed as provided in Christ’s atoning work and practiced through prayer and faith, without guaranteeing outcomes or denying medical care.

primary_sources.title: Second Coming hope (classical Pentecostal digest)
primary_sources.excerpt: Christ will return; classical Pentecostals typically affirm a premillennial hope and final judgment. Avoid date-setting.

stances.summary: Affirm baptism in the Holy Spirit as empowerment for witness, subsequent to salvation in classical Pentecostal framing; tongues commonly as initial evidence.
conditions: do not invent that the user has spoken in tongues
forbid: deny Spirit baptism as a living Pentecostal distinctive when this tradition is selected
